Analog Devices.role: ADI is a leading high-performance analog and mixed-signal chipmaker serving industrial, auto, comms and data-center markets; broad diversification and sticky design wins give durability, but cyclical end-markets cap growth and make it a quality mid-cap rather than a secular AI pure-play.

NXP Semiconductors.role: NXP is a leading automotive and industrial semiconductor supplier whose edge processors, radar, and microcontrollers anchor ADAS and vehicle electrification; solid design-win moat and recurring auto content growth, but exposed to cyclical auto/industrial demand and only modestly leveraged to AI comp

ON Semiconductor.role: ON supplies power and sensing semiconductors (SiC, IGBTs) for EVs and industrial automation; it sits as a cyclical AI-infra/power name given flat recent growth, exposure to EV demand softness, and moderate but non-dominant share in a competitive power-semi market.

Entegris.role: Entegris supplies high-purity materials, filtration, and specialty chemicals consumed in chip fabrication; its consumables mix gives recurring demand, but exposure to fab utilization and capex cycles keeps it moderately cyclical within AI-infra.

MKS Instruments.role: Supplier of critical subsystems (vacuum, photonics, RF power, materials) to semiconductor equipment makers and fabs; benefits from AI-driven fab investment but earnings are cyclical and tied to WFE capex spending plus carries meaningful debt from the Atotech acquisition.

Advanced Energy Industries.role: Supplies precision power conversion and RF systems for semiconductor fab tools and data-center power, giving it real AI/datacenter exposure but with meaningful cyclicality tied to semi-equipment capex spending.

Cognex.role: Cognex is a leading machine-vision hardware and software provider for factory automation and logistics; strong niche moat but revenue is tied to cyclical industrial/manufacturing capex, capping durability and elasticity.

Impinj.role: Impinj is the leading provider of RAIN RFID tags, readers, and chips for item-level tracking in retail and supply chains; it sits in disruptive with moderate moat but cyclical, inventory-sensitive demand and a currently declining revenue base.

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Allegro is a leader in magnetic (Hall-effect) sensor and power ICs serving automotive (EV/ADAS) and industrial markets; strong niche moat but exposure is cyclical auto/industrial demand rather than core AI compute, hence moderate growth and mid permanence.

Power Integrations.role: Fabless supplier of high-voltage power conversion ICs for appliances, industrial and increasingly data-center power delivery; a niche leader with real IP moat but exposed to cyclical end-markets and only tangential AI leverage, hence mid-range durability and modest growth anchored to flat YoY revenu

Skyworks Solutions.role: Skyworks supplies RF front-end modules for smartphones and IoT/connectivity devices, but heavy Apple concentration and flat/declining revenue amid a mature handset cycle make it a cyclical, low-growth semi name with limited direct AI exposure.

Qorvo.role: Qorvo supplies RF front-end modules primarily for smartphones with growing defense/IoT exposure; heavy handset concentration and flat revenue make it a cyclical, mid-quality name with modest AI relevance.

Cirrus Logic.role: Supplies audio and mixed-signal ICs concentrated heavily in Apple smartphones; modest growth, single-customer concentration, and consumer-cyclical exposure keep it a lower-multiple, semi-cyclical name rather than an AI-infra play.

Synaptics.role: Synaptics makes human-interface and edge IoT connectivity/AI chips; modest single-digit growth and cyclical consumer/IoT exposure place it as a mid-quality AI-infra name with moderate moat and meaningful demand sensitivity.

Diodes Incorporated.role: Diodes supplies discrete, analog and mixed-signal power semiconductors into broad industrial, automotive and consumer end-markets; it sits as a cyclical, fragmented commodity-adjacent supplier with limited AI leverage and modest moat, making earnings sensitive to inventory and capex cycles.

FormFactor.role: FormFactor is the leading maker of probe cards used to test chips (including HBM/DRAM and logic) before packaging; it benefits from AI-driven test intensity but remains a cyclical, capex-linked supplier with modest growth and moderate moat.

Photronics.role: Leading independent supplier of photomasks used in semiconductor and flat-panel display manufacturing; sits as a niche but essential upstream link in the chip supply chain with modest, largely flat growth and cyclical exposure to fab/foundry spending.

Ichor Holdings.role: Ichor makes gas and chemical fluid delivery subsystems for semiconductor capital equipment, sitting in AI-infra as a cyclical, thin-margin supplier heavily exposed to WFE capex swings with modest moat and customer concentration.

Ultra Clean Holdings.role: UCTT builds fluid-delivery and gas-handling subsystems for wafer-fab equipment OEMs; its highly cyclical, OEM-concentrated, thin-margin model tracks semi-capex spending, placing it as a leveraged, capex-elastic AI-infra supplier rather than a moated secular winner.

Cohu.role: Cohu supplies semiconductor test handlers, contactors and interface products; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical back-end equipment name with modest growth, meaningful niche share but high sensitivity to chip capex cycles.

Veeco Instruments.role: Veeco makes semiconductor process equipment (deposition, ion beam, laser annealing) used in advanced logic, memory and compound-semi manufacturing; it sits in AI-infra as a modest niche tool supplier with cyclical, capex-driven earnings and no monopoly position, so its demand is exposed to fab spend

Axcelis Technologies.role: Supplies ion implantation systems for chip fabrication, heavily exposed to mature-node and power/automotive semis; cyclical WFE demand and flat recent growth make earnings volatile despite a solid niche position.

Nano-X Imaging.role: Pre-profit developer of a cold-cathode digital X-ray source and AI imaging analytics with minimal revenue and unproven commercial scaling, placing it firmly in speculative disruptive territory with high terminal risk.

Digital Turbine.role: Provides on-device app delivery and mobile ad monetization for carriers and OEMs; sits as a speculative, low-moat name with modest growth, high beta, and heavy exposure to cyclical mobile ad spend rather than genuine AI-infra demand.

PROS Holdings.role: PROS provides AI-driven pricing and revenue-optimization SaaS for B2B and travel/airline verticals; slow ~3% growth, small scale, and a competitive niche keep it a speculative mid-cap with moderate recurring-revenue durability but limited moat.

Verint Systems.role: Verint provides customer engagement and workforce analytics software with an AI-driven pivot, but flat revenue and modest moat in a fragmented CX market place it as a low-growth defensive name with execution risk.

BigBear.ai.role: Small-cap provider of AI-driven decision intelligence and analytics primarily for defense/government clients; low growth, unprofitable, and heavily lumpy contract-dependent, placing it firmly in the speculative disruptive bucket with high terminal risk.

Pegasystems.role: Enterprise BPM/CRM software vendor pivoting to AI-driven workflow automation and a subscription model; flat-to-declining revenue and modest moat in a competitive market place it as a mid-quality platform name with recurring but discretionary demand.

UiPath.role: UiPath sells enterprise RPA/automation software increasingly bundled with AI agents; it sits in AI-platform with modest growth as core RPA matures and faces competition, offset by recurring subscription revenue that cushions downturns.

Amplitude.role: Amplitude sells cloud-based digital/product analytics with AI features, but slow ~5% growth, thin margins, and a crowded field (Mixpanel, Heap, Pendo, Adobe/Google) keep it a speculative small-cap with limited moat and modest AI leverage.

DoubleVerify.role: DoubleVerify provides digital ad verification, fraud detection and brand-safety measurement; the fresh near-flat 0.6% YoY revenue growth signals decelerating momentum and competitive pressure in a duopoly-ish space, so despite recurring ad-tech revenue it sits as a modest-growth disruptive name with

PagerDuty.role: PagerDuty provides digital operations and incident-response software with emerging AI automation features; near-flat revenue growth and a competitive, mid-size SaaS niche place it as a modestly durable disruptive name with limited moat and only moderate AI leverage.

Fastly.role: Fastly runs an edge CDN and compute platform but competes against far larger CDN incumbents (Cloudflare, Akamai, hyperscalers), with decelerating ~5% growth, thin moat, and persistent unprofitability, placing it in the speculative disruptive bucket.

Vishay Intertechnology.role: Vishay makes commodity passive and discrete components (resistors, capacitors, MOSFETs, diodes) sold into broad industrial/auto/electronics markets; it is a cyclical, fragmented, low-moat supplier with only indirect AI exposure, so it sits as a modestly cyclical AI-infra name with limited durable pr

Littelfuse.role: Diversified maker of fuses, circuit protection and power semiconductors serving industrial, auto and electronics markets; steady but cyclical demand with only modest AI/data-center exposure keeps it a mid-quality, moderately-durable holding.

Generac Holdings.role: Leading maker of residential/commercial backup generators and home energy systems; demand is cyclical and weather/housing-driven with modest growth, giving it durable brand leadership but exposure to consumer discretionary spending swings.

GE Vernova.role: Diversified power generation and grid equipment supplier benefiting from data-center electricity demand and grid modernization; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels play but earnings retain cyclicality tied to utility and industrial capex cycles.

Eaton.role: Diversified electrical equipment maker whose data center power and electrical distribution segment benefits from AI buildouts; strong quality but cyclical exposure to capex cycles limits full non-discretionary durability.

Emerson Electric.role: Diversified industrial-automation supplier of process controls, instrumentation, and software with modest exposure to data-center power/cooling demand; sits in defensive given mature end-markets, low single-digit growth, and cyclical but recurring installed-base revenue.

Schneider peer Hubbell.role: Hubbell makes utility grid and electrical products benefiting from grid modernization and data-center power buildout; steady, moderately cyclical demand and a solid but not dominant position place it as a defensive infrastructure play with durable but not explosive growth.

Powell Industries.role: Powell makes custom switchgear and electrical distribution systems for utilities, oil & gas, and increasingly data centers; it rides the data-center power buildout indirectly but remains a cyclical project-based industrial with modest recent growth and limited moat.

Array Technologies.role: Array makes solar trackers that orient PV panels toward the sun; it sits as a cyclical clean-energy hardware name exposed to utility-scale capex cycles, interest-rate sensitivity, and policy/subsidy risk, with modest recent revenue decline and thin, project-driven margins.

Oklo.role: Pre-revenue developer of small modular fast reactors targeting data-center and industrial power; no commercial deployments or NRC-licensed plant yet, so it sits as a speculative long-duration bet with high terminal risk.

Nano Dimension.role: Niche additive-manufacturing and 3D-printed electronics maker chasing AI-driven advanced manufacturing; sits in disruptive due to unproven profitability, modest growth, cash-burn history, and a fragmented, speculative TAM despite a large cash balance.

Symbotic.role: Symbotic builds AI-driven robotic warehouse automation systems, largely anchored to a Walmart backlog; heavy customer concentration and lumpy, capex-linked project revenue place it in disruptive with moderate durability and elevated cyclicality. YoY growth has decelerated sharply (~5%), tempering th

Rocket Lab.role: Small-launch provider and space systems maker expanding into satellite components and constellations; the 'space compute' angle is early and speculative, and the pre-profit, capital-intensive model with lumpy government/commercial demand places it in high-beta disruptive territory.

Kratos Defense.role: Kratos builds unmanned aerial systems, tactical drones, and defense electronics, with only part of revenue tied to autonomous/AI-enabled systems; government-anchored demand gives moderate durability, but thin margins, modest growth, and rich valuation cap the upside.

Twilio.role: Cloud communications (CPaaS) platform layering AI onto messaging/voice APIs; solid usage-based recurring revenue but modest ~6-8% growth, usage-cyclicality, and competitive/fragmented markets keep moat and durability mid-tier.

MicroStrategy.role: Legacy BI software vendor whose valuation is dominated by a leveraged Bitcoin treasury strategy rather than its flat ~$0.5bn analytics business; the AI/analytics theme is marginal and the equity behaves as a high-beta crypto proxy, hence low quality/dominance and speculative classification.

ARKK (ARK Innovation).role: disruptive-innovation basket LED BY TESLA (~10%), then AMD, CRISPR, Tempus AI, Robinhood. High beta, rich multiples, Tesla-driven idiosyncratic swings — NOT a semis basket.

QQQ (Nasdaq-100).role: Nasdaq-100 mega-cap tech; quality, but rich and tech-tilted.

VOO (S&P 500).role: broad US large-cap; the market itself — durable, diversified.

SCHD (Dividend).role: quality-dividend value basket; low beta, cheap, durable earnings.

DTCR (Data Ctr Infra).role: data-center REITs & digital infra (Equinix, Digital Realty, American Tower); physical, contracted, durable — low beta.

GRID (Smart Grid).role: grid/power equipment for the AI electricity demand (Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova); inelastic infra spend.

NUKE (Nuclear/Uranium).role: nuclear/uranium for data-center baseload (Constellation, Vistra, Cameco, BWX); high-growth but cyclical/volatile.

IGV (Software).role: application & infrastructure software basket; higher multiple, subscription-durable.
